claims.text: Recruiting - Morgan Stanley: no advisor-recruiting statement from Morgan Stanley is in the evidence provided (see gaps).

Recruiting - Merrill: On the 1Q25 Bank of America earnings call (April 2025), the CFO said GWIM expense growth of 9% supported, among other things, the cost of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the private bank.

Recruiting - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes roles designed to help advisors meet clients, identify financial goals, align banking and investing solutions and build a book of high-net-worth clients. It pitches a career in wealth management with 'unlimited growth and earning potential'.

Recruiting - Merrill: Trade press (published 2026-11-16) reports that Merrill executives in October touted recruited assets to the wealth unit doubling year over year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting. It says Merrill largely pulled back from veteran recruiting at the end of 2017, and that Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. It also lists recent hires from UBS, Morgan Stanley and Edward Jones. This is trade-press reporting, not a firm filing.

Recruiting - Raymond James: On the fiscal 4Q25 call (October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year. He cited a robust recruiting pipeline and strong commitments to join in coming quarters, and said the 'best-of-both-worlds' value proposition resonates across all affiliation options. He also named the firm's balance sheet and commitment to independence as differentiators.
Recruiting - Raymond James: In its fiscal 2Q26 earnings release (April 22, 2026), the CEO said financial advisor recruiting activity across all affiliation options 'remains robust'.

Recruiting - Raymond James: The 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 (published August 2026) cites compensation costs tied to growth, including financial advisor recruiting and retention-related compensation expenses. It also cites financial advisor recruiting-related expenses in non-compensation costs. It attributes net new assets to financial advisor recruiting and retention.
Retention - Morgan Stanley: no advisor-retention statement from Morgan Stanley is in the evidence provided (see gaps).
Retention - Merrill: no Merrill advisor-retention statement is in the evidence provided (see gaps).

Retention - Raymond James: On the fiscal 4Q25 call (October 2025), the CEO described the record advisor count as reflecting 'solid advisor retention' as well as strong recruiting. He said the firm continues to invest in its platform and offerings to retain and attract advisors.

Retention - Raymond James: The fiscal 2025 10-K (published November 2025) names advisor departures as a risk, including to independent RIAs, some backed by private equity, which has produced a 'highly competitive recruiting environment'. It says reported AUA may be negatively affected if the firm fails to retain or recruit advisors. The firm says it seeks to mitigate this through financial advisor succession planning and a broad range of services and resources to support advisors' practices.

adjacent.text: The Morgan Stanley 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) says its talent development programs are designed to help employees achieve career goals, and that the firm believes supporting employee development and growth contributes to long-term retention.
adjacent.differs_because: It describes talent development for all employees, not advisor recruiting or retention specifically.

adjacent.text: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Morgan Stanley's CFO described greater retention of vested Workplace assets and migration of those assets to advice.
adjacent.differs_because: It concerns retention of client assets from the Workplace channel, not retention of advisors.
